fact: RobotsMali AI4D Lab published two open-source Bambara speech-recognition models, Soloni-114M TDT-CTC and QuartzNet-15x5, trained on about 35 hours of Bambara audio, with weights on Hugging Face.

RobotsMali AI4D Lab in Bamako released 612 hours of transcribed Bambara speech, fine-tuned ASR models (Parakeet and QuartzNet based, deployed in the An Be Kalan app) and the 45-recording Nyana-Eval benchmark, as part of African Next Voices.
